# Humanizer — detect and rewrite AI writing tells in five voice profiles

Curated by Skill Harbor — @aboudjem's humanizer: an editing skill that hunts 55 documented AI writing patterns (significance inflation, superficial -ing phrases, vocabulary tells like "delve" and "tapestry", em-dash overuse, uniform sentence length, and more), scores the text 0–100, and rewrites it in one of five voice profiles — casual, professional, technical, warm, blunt. Three modes: detect (report only), rewrite (full transform with a before/after change summary), and edit (in-place Markdown editing). The guardrails are the real craft: flag pattern clusters, never isolated tells; never rewrite quoted, code, or cited content; protect non-native-English and neurodivergent prose styles; never fabricate facts. Honest caveats: it's an editor, not a verdict — the score is a signal, not proof of authorship; pure Markdown, zero dependencies, no network calls; prose only, not code. MIT licensed. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
